div.head: Ps Cn for 21.2
div.ab: nam crimen ueneris ab antiquo inter maiora et non immerito numerabatur, uiridis uero, fractione chacee nostre regalis excepta, ita pusillum et exiguum est, quod uix ea respicit nostra constitutio; qui in hoc tamen deliquerit, sit criminis foreste reus.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 623 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: for the crime of venison was from of old, and not undeservedly, counted among the greater [crimes], but [that] of vert, except for breach of our royal chase, is so small and slight that our ordinance scarcely regards it; yet whoever offends in this, let him be guilty of a forest crime.

note.seg: Im 13. Jh. hat chacea die technische Bed.: ‘Privaten überlassener Forst’ (Turner p. cix), hier offenbar noch nicht. — Nur vor viridarii und forestarii, aber nicht vor die Reiserichter kamen die Klagen wegen Holzschlag im Forst im 13. Jh.; Turner p. xxxiii ff.

In the 13th century chacea has the technical meaning ‘forest left to private persons’ (Turner p. cix), here evidently not yet. — In the 13th century complaints about felling wood in the forest came only before the viridarii and forestarii, not before the itinerant justices; Turner p. xxxiii ff.
